newsitem.title: CHINA: HK bishop urges China to seek "spirit of democracy".
newsitem.headline: HK bishop urges China to seek "spirit of democracy".

text.p: Hong Kong's Roman Catholic church on Tuesday called on China to embrace more spiritual values and democracy as worshipers attended their first mass after the territory's handover to Beijing.

"Together with our compatriots, we want our country to move forward from a material to a spiritual civilisation to open up in a spirit of democracy and the rule of law...to find the true meaning of human life," Bishop John Tong said in a sermon.
He made the remarks in a mass at the Catholic Cathedral to mark Hong Kong's first day under communist Chinese rule.
The bishop called on people in Hong Kong to love their compatriots in mainland China who have been separated from the territory for the past 156 years.
China ceded Hong Kong to Britain in 1841 after winning wars with China over opium trade. London handed the territory back to Beijing at midnight on Monday.
Hundreds of faithful flocked to the mass, which was presided over by Hong Kong prelate Cardinal John Baptist Wu. The congregation prayed for God to bless Hong Kong and China.
During the mass Cardinal Wu read out a letter from the Pope.
The pontiff sent his blessing to Hong Kong and Chinese Catholics last week, wishing them well for the handover.
Hong Kong has about 250,000 Catholics among a population of 6.4 million, nearly all Chinese.
Officially atheist China has promised to respect religion, among other aspects of Hong Kong's way of life, for 50 years.
But the Beijing government does not recognise the ultimate authority of the Vatican in religious affairs.
It insists Catholics in China worship under the auspices of a state-controlled Catholic Patriotic Association.
